content.title: Mixed-Media Ensemble | Distinct Character Modules Converge
content.summary: Build at least four self-contained style modules. Each module must introduce one original character, one material or line-behavior rule, and one short action that could not be explained by color grading alone. Connect modules with one repeated composition slot, emblem position or motion direction. In the final beat, bring the intact characters into one neutral shared stage while preserving each character's original medium, edge behavior and surface response.

quick_start.input_format: Give every module one different original character and one medium-specific material rule. + Include one short action that visibly demonstrates each medium's behavior. + Repeat one composition slot, emblem position or motion direction across modules. + Keep each outgoing character readable until the next module's anchor arrives. + Converge intact heterogeneous characters on one neutral stage without restyling them uniformly.
quick_start.recommended_input: Open on an original ceramic stop-motion transit mascot on a numbered plinth; one small step leaves a tactile clay compression and establishes the first medium rule. A cut-paper relief fox unfolds one layered tail, then an original wireframe-light turtle traces one volumetric arc; each receives a full readable module and one medium-specific action. Bring all five intact mascots onto the same neutral platform: ceramic compression, graphite grain, paper layers, light wires and embroidery remain distinct. Hold the ensemble with one original mark ROUTE FIVE and no source characters or style labels.

usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.

Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Build at least four self-contained style modules. not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Build at least four self-contained style modules. Each module must introduce one original character, one material or line-behavior rule, and one short action that could not be explained by color grading alone. Connect modules with one repeated composition slot, emblem position or motion direction. In the final beat, bring the intact characters into one neutral shared stage while preserving each character's original medium, edge behavior and surface response. The reusable mechanism is medium-specific proof, matched modular handoff and heterogeneous ensemble convergence—not the source characters, named styles, exact order, cards, text, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Give every module one different original character and one medium-specific material rule.
invariants.purpose: Separates genuine style construction from palette swapping.
invariants.ablation_failure: The same render with filters cannot prove cross-medium design.

invariants.rule: Include one short action that visibly demonstrates each medium's behavior.
invariants.ablation_failure: Static portraits provide weak transfer evidence.

invariants.rule: Repeat one composition slot, emblem position or motion direction across modules.
invariants.purpose: Creates continuity despite radical surface changes.
invariants.ablation_failure: Unmatched cards read as unrelated samples.

invariants.rule: Keep each outgoing character readable until the next module's anchor arrives.
invariants.purpose: Makes transitions attributable rather than abrupt.

invariants.rule: Converge intact heterogeneous characters on one neutral stage without restyling them uniformly.
invariants.purpose: Proves co-presence and completes the system.
invariants.ablation_failure: A final common filter erases the central difference.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: source warriors and representative character designs
source clay, painted, ink, storybook and comic executions in their exact order
source captions, style labels, logos and typography
source module layouts, transitions and final ensemble staging
source MiniMax H3 creator identity, prompt thread and timing
